reason: Both correctly refuse a retry and tell the homeowner to keep it isolated and get an engineer, but Conversation 2 gives a far more complete safety boundary: check for residual heat/smouldering, call 999 and evacuate if smoke or flames return, tape off the spur, don't open panels, plus a sensible recall check and photo documentation for insurance. Conversation 1 wastes its first reply asking the user to open the door and inspect for standing water and a blocked filter right after a smoke event, which is an unnecessary and mildly unsafe question given the burning panel, and never covers what to do if smoke recurs. Conversation 2 did stop after one turn without following up on the reported scorch mark, and its 911/112 mention is slightly off for a UK user, but its single response was more thorough and better prioritised than Conversation 1's two.
